To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RMI system is not designed for mobile hosts with intermittently available connections and that it can be extended to handle this scenario.
the Java RMI protocol is not suitable for use with intermittent connections, and that a new protocol is needed.

the Java RMI framework can be extended to support the following: 1) a new communication model that is based on a logical connection, 2) a new communication protocol for establishing and maintaining a connection, and 3) a new communication mechanism that supports a connection-based communication model and a connection-oriented communication protocol.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design of a remote object system which can be used to develop mobile applications that are oblivious of the communication link failure, and which are able to choose the most suitable policy for a particular situation.
the following questions: (a) How can we provide an infrastructure for mobile hosts that supports a variety of policies to handle intermittent connectivity?

structuring the remote object system so that it can be used in a variety of situations, and with providing a clean separation between application functionality and policies for handling the effects of link failures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a distributed object system for mobile hosts is not a panacea for the problem of intermittent connectivity.
we have shown that the Java RMI can be extended to handle link failures in a way that is transparent to applications.
the proposed system provides the necessary tools to build applications that can be deployed on a wide variety of platforms and environments, and still be robust to link failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to decouple the effects of intermittent communication from the application and provide a clean interface for application developers.
the application is oblivious of the link failure, and the link failure handling is oblivious of the application.
we have developed a framework to support a variety of policies for handling link failures in mobile hosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application is decoupled from the communication infrastructure, and can be deployed in different environments without any changes.
the application is no longer tied to a particular communication infrastructure and that it can adapt to a changing environment.
it is possible to structure remote object systems so that the application is not aware of communication failures and can be used in a variety of different network environments.
